title: What everyone gets WRONG about bodyfat %
summary: He argues body fat percentage matters less than how you look, measurements are inaccurate, and muscle mass changes how a given percentage looks. Self-reporting is skewed (overweight people understate, lean people claim single digits), which distorts perceptions and FFMI-based natural limit debates. Naturals should live around 12-18%.
claims: At 210 lb he sits around 17-18% body fat; he could be 180 or 225 lb at the same percentage and look like a completely different person while carrying different amounts of fat
Knowing your exact body fat percentage is useless; nobody asks for it, what matters is how you look
No body fat measurement method is accurate, and in the 15-20% range each percent of error changes the picture a lot
On a large lean mass, trading 2% body fat for muscle at the same weight makes you look immensely better
Online critics guessed him at about 12% from a video when he is actually 16-17%
Two people at 17% body fat look different: the one with more muscle looks leaner because muscle makes fat look more evenly distributed
Lifters mainly gain subcutaneous fat around the muscles rather than visceral fat; the trained body places fat around muscles as a spring and sleeve for resilience
Body fat norms are built on the wrong people, untrained individuals, and skewed by those who obsess and publicise their numbers
Like men inflating their height, overweight men understate body fat, so YouTube fitness thinks 17-18% looks obese; people doubt he is 6 ft for the same reason
At 17-18% he has a full six-pack and visible obliques
Guys at 13-14% claim under 10%; real 8% means striations and feathering, and abs plus biceps veins do not mean single digits
Understating body fat by 4-5% inflates FFMI calculations to 26-27, which ruins the natural limit discussion
Natural lifters should stay between about 12% and 18% body fat, some 10-12% or 18-20%; build muscle in that range rather than starving yourself
Naturals cannot maintain their hormones when very lean like enhanced athletes, so the trend of naturals stepping on stage super skinny should stop
